speaker: I. A. Batalin
title: First-class constraints and structure functions
summary: The dated block on P000866 introduces first-class constraints, asks whether their structure functions can be made constant, and writes a multiplier action. The catalogue attributes it to Batalin; the notebook's tentative \ru{Некто (Батурин)} is retained as an attribution uncertainty. The catalogue's overlapping P000864--P000867 interval is not a literal boundary: the new block starts on P000866 and ends before Kallosh's heading on that page.

speaker: Renata Kallosh
title: Background-field quantization, ghosts and gauge dependence
summary: Kallosh relates formal generating functionals and scattering amplitudes, then presents background-field gauge fixing for gravity, ghost terms, and an on-shell gauge-independence argument. Maxwell theory supplies a transparent example of gauge degeneracy. Several formulas suppress normalization, loop order, or curvature terms. The supergravity discussion concerns gauge-algebra and ghost modifications; it does not claim ultraviolet finiteness.

speaker: I. A. Batalin
title: Faddeev--Popov reduction and BRST invariance
summary: The scan on P000871 dates this lecture \ru{29/X-79}, so 29 October is used here; the supplied catalogue's 29 September is recorded as a provenance discrepancy. After stationary phase and Maxwell gauge degeneracy, a finite-dimensional group-action model derives the gauge-slice determinant and ghost representation. BRST transformations, physical unitarity, gauge independence, open supergravity algebras and the Yang--Mills example follow. The notes are an exposition of methods circulating before the talk, not an instance of the later odd-antibracket BV formalism.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Gravity, Einstein metrics and the gravitational boundary action
summary: The heading says \ru{По Хокингу}. Gelfand compares approaches to quantum gravity, writes the Einstein--Hilbert variational problem, mentions Yau, and motivates the gravitational boundary term and reference subtraction. The notebook's purported universal uniqueness theorem for Einstein metrics is substantially false. The corrected Kähler statements are identified with Yau's 1977 announcement/1978 proof; the boundary action matches Gibbons--Hawking 1977.

speaker: I. A. Batalin
title: Graded constraints, Dirac brackets and phase-space measures
summary: The lecture develops graded canonical brackets, first- and second-class constraints, reduction by Dirac brackets, and the phase-space path integral. Gelfand recognizes the Dirac bracket as the inverse of the induced symplectic form. Source-generating equations lead to a formal constrained integral with the square-root Berezinian; adding gauge conditions makes a regular first-class system second class. These are pre-existing Hamiltonian methods, with a contemporaneous 1977/1978 graded extension.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Dilogarithms and six proposed connections
summary: The dated introductory page asks where dilogarithms occur and lists six areas, then writes an integral and a differential five-term relation. The catalogue attributes this introduction to Gelfand, although the page itself says only Gelfand seminar. In the actual notebook it precedes Beilinson's P000885--P000886 contribution (record 476); the catalogue numbers reverse that order. The list is a research map, not six fully formulated conjectures.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Dilogarithms, tame symbols and regulators of curves
summary: Beilinson explains the real dilogarithmic regulator, its Steinberg identity and tame-symbol periods, then refines it to a complex multiplicative regulator. The latter matches his short 1980 publication closely. The opening remark about zeta functions has no sufficiently precise arithmetic conjecture. Source errors include the sign of the zeta(2) integral, a missing period normalization, and calling a multiplicative skew symbol symmetric. The distinction between K-theory of the curve and its function field is essential.

speaker: I. A. Batalin
title: Hamiltonian BRST quantization in a relativistic gauge
summary: The second Batalin contribution on 19 November extends phase space by multiplier momenta and ghosts, introduces an odd nilpotent BRST charge and a gauge fermion, and sketches gauge independence by a field-dependent BRST change of variables. This is the contemporaneous Hamiltonian BFV framework, whose even Poisson bracket must be distinguished from the later BV antibracket. The statement about termination of supergravity ghost expansions remains model dependent.

speaker: I. Yu. Kobzarev
title: Elementary particles, gauge representations and the Higgs potential
summary: The speaker is called physicist in this block and identified as Kobzarev by the catalogue and the following lecture's tentative name. The talk surveys quark and lepton charges, three generations, colour and chiral weak representations, gauge-boson exchange and a gauge-invariant scalar potential. It is exposition of pre-existing physics rather than a new theorem announcement. Its massless-neutrino language and unobserved top quark are retained as 1979 context, with current status distinguished.

speaker: I. Yu. Kobzarev
title: Confinement heuristics and the electroweak mass mechanism
summary: The continuation first contrasts Coulomb fields with a proposed chromoelectric tube, with a short intervention attributed to Manin. It then derives the scalar Hessian, symmetry zero modes, gauge-boson masses, the Higgs-doublet breaking pattern, weak mixing, currents and fermion masses, ending with the quark mixing matrix. The confinement picture is distinguished from its still-open four-dimensional continuum formulation. The Higgs and weak-interaction material is principally exposition of older results, with explicit corrections to several notebook formulas.
